seen.where: Benson StoryMap 'Corresponding with Pancho Villa' https://storymaps.arcgis.com/stories/87a0c4340f634e01b75d3e603d9946dd, section 'Coded Writing' (images and text opened in Chrome 4 Nov 2026); item list from the TARO guide https://txarchives.org/utlac/finding_aids/00075.xml (Guide to the Lazaro de la Garza Archive, UT Austin Benson Latin American Collection; opened in Chrome 4 Nov 2026, item descriptions counted by script).
seen.extent: TARO item descriptions: 54 items described exactly '[In code.]', 88 'Partly in code', 5 'In code, with a translation' (plus 'Partly in code, with a translation'), about 165 dated 1913-15, telegrams and letters Villa <-> de la Garza. The StoryMap shows a few sample sheets only (5-character groups on grid paper, key sheets, a typed decoded message on Division of the North letterhead).
seen.cipher: TARO: '[In code.]' (54 items), '[Partly in code, concerning General Gonzalez; the note concerns attacks on Torreon and Monterrey.]', '[Asking him not to send telegrams in code because he does not have the key.]', '[Asking de la Garza to repeat a coded message which Villa could not decipher.]'. StoryMap: 'De la Garza always parsed out his writing in 5-character sets, and sometimes identified at the start of the letter the number of the corresponding key Villa should use to decode the message.' The sample sheets shown carry contemporary decipherments (grid-paper working, typed decoded text); those exemplars are read and are excluded. For the items described only as 'In code.' no decipherment is listed in the guide.

2226.note: Three letters of Maria Christierna to her mother (Fogaras 2 Aug 1597; 11 and 20 Dec 1597) printed in MTT XXIII (1877) with the cipher replaced by '(Chiffre)' and a note that the keys were not found, so only about six short number passages inside clear German text survive in the Vienna originals (offline); weak target.

seen.where: Szilagyi Sandor, 'Okmanyok es levelek az 1595-1598-ki pragai alkudozasok tortenetehez, a becsi cs. k. allamlevéltarban levo eredetiekbol', Magyar Tortenelmi Tar XXIII (Budapest 1877) pp. 149-239 (Lang's 'MTT II/11'), letters VII (pp. 162-163), XXIX (pp. 181-183), XXXII (pp. 186-187); read from the Google scan on Internet Archive https://archive.org/details/magyartrtnelmit01bizogoog (djvu text, 4 Nov 2026). The originals are in Vienna (state archive) and not online; the lead has no access field, and nothing found shows an image of them.
seen.extent: Three letters, German; the printed text has six cipher passages of a word or short phrase each: two in the letter of 2 Aug 1597 (Fogaras), two in 11 Dec 1597, two in 20 Dec 1597. Lang's repertory p. 253 describes them as 'nemet szamok, nehany reszleges' (German numbers, a few partial signs) and 'megfejtetlen'.
seen.cipher: The edition does not print the ciphertext: it substitutes '(Chiffre)' in the running text (e.g. 'dann (Chiffre) wirt gar vngeduldig' in 11 Dec 1597; 'allain das (Chiffre) zu Deuen auf des (Chiffre) Schloss ist' in 2 Aug 1597), and under the 2 Aug letter adds 'A titkos jegyek kulcsai nem voltak feltalalhatok' (the keys of the secret signs could not be found). No decipherment is written on or with the letters in the edition; the clear German context makes the hidden words guessable.
